items.question: Which picture shows a push?
options: A child pushing a toy car
A child watching a toy car
A child sitting next to a toy car
A child picking up a toy car
items.correct_answer: A child pushing a toy car
items.explanation: A push moves an object away from you. When a child pushes a toy car, they are using force to move it forward.

items.question: Draw a picture showing how you could make a ball move far and how you could make it move a short distance. Label your pictures.

rubric.4: Two clear pictures showing strong/weak push with accurate labels and explanation
rubric.3: Two pictures with labels showing different force levels
rubric.2: Pictures present but labels or force difference unclear
rubric.1: Attempted drawing but concept not demonstrated

items.question: Sara wants to make her toy car go faster. What should she do?
items.explanation: A stronger push gives an object more speed. Pushing harder makes the car go faster.

items.question: You have a ramp and a toy car. Tell how you would test if the car goes faster when you push it hard or push it soft. What would you look at to know which push was stronger?

rubric.4: Clear procedure with comparison of two push strengths and observable outcome (distance or speed)
rubric.3: Procedure mentions both push types but observation method less clear
rubric.2: Basic idea of testing but incomplete procedure
rubric.1: Mentions pushing but no comparison or observation method

items.question: What do ALL plants need to live?
items.explanation: All plants need water and sunlight to survive. These help plants make their food and grow.

items.question: Look at a picture of a dog and a fish. Draw what each animal needs to survive. Are any needs the same?

rubric.4: Identifies specific needs for both animals and correctly identifies water/food as common needs
rubric.3: Shows needs for both animals with some common needs identified
rubric.2: Shows needs but common elements not identified
rubric.1: Shows items but not clearly related to survival needs

items.question: How do beavers change the land where they live?
options: They build dams that create ponds
They fly high in the sky
They swim without touching the water
They hide underground all the time
items.correct_answer: They build dams that create ponds
items.explanation: Beavers change their environment by building dams out of sticks and mud. This creates ponds where they can live safely.

items.question: Think about birds making nests. How do birds change the environment to meet their needs? Draw a picture and tell about it.

rubric.4: Picture and explanation show how birds gather materials and build nests for shelter/eggs with clear connection to needs
rubric.3: Shows nest building with some connection to bird needs
rubric.2: Shows nest but limited connection to needs
rubric.1: Drawing of bird but nest or needs not clear

items.question: Which words describe weather?
items.explanation: Weather describes what is happening outside with the sky, temperature, and wind. Sunny, rainy, and windy are all types of weather.

items.question: For one week, draw a picture of the weather each day. What pattern did you see? Was the weather the same or different each day?

rubric.4: Weather recorded for multiple days with pattern identified and described
rubric.3: Weather recorded with attempt to identify pattern
rubric.2: Weather recorded but no pattern discussion

items.question: Where would a polar bear live best?
items.explanation: Polar bears need cold places to live because they have thick fur to keep warm in snow and ice. They find food and make homes in cold areas.

items.question: Draw a fish in its home. What does the fish need in its home to survive? Why does the fish live there and not on land?

rubric.4: Drawing shows water habitat with explanation of fish needs (water, food, shelter) and why water is necessary
rubric.3: Shows fish in water with some needs identified
rubric.2: Fish in water but needs not clearly explained

items.question: Why do we check the weather forecast before going outside?
options: To know if we need an umbrella or jacket
To know what color to wear
To know what games to play inside
To know what food to eat
items.correct_answer: To know if we need an umbrella or jacket
items.explanation: Weather forecasts help us prepare for conditions like rain or cold. This helps us stay safe and comfortable.

items.question: A big storm is coming to your town. What would you and your family do to get ready? Draw and tell about it.

rubric.4: Shows multiple preparation actions (staying inside, gathering supplies, securing items) with clear explanation
rubric.1: Response relates to storms but preparation not clear

items.question: Which action helps keep the Earth clean?
options: Putting trash in a garbage can
items.correct_answer: Putting trash in a garbage can
items.explanation: Putting trash in proper containers keeps litter off the ground and helps protect plants, animals, and water.

items.question: Think of one way people hurt the land, water, or air. Draw a solution that would help make it better.

rubric.4: Identifies problem clearly and proposes logical solution with drawing and explanation
rubric.3: Shows problem and solution with some explanation
rubric.2: Shows either problem or solution but not both clearly
rubric.1: Drawing present but connection to environmental issue unclear

items.question: The class needs a way to carry books from the library. What question should they ask first?
options: How many books do we need to carry?
What color should our carrier be?
items.correct_answer: How many books do we need to carry?
items.explanation: To solve a problem, we first need to understand it. Knowing how many books helps us design something that will work.

items.question: The classroom pet hamster needs a new toy to play with. What questions would you ask before making a toy for the hamster?

rubric.4: Multiple relevant questions about hamster size, safety, what hamsters like, materials available
rubric.3: At least two relevant questions about the problem
rubric.2: One relevant question with some connection to problem
rubric.1: Questions present but not related to design problem

items.question: You want to make a cup that will not spill. Which shape would work best?
options: A tall cup with a lid
items.correct_answer: A tall cup with a lid
items.explanation: A tall cup can hold liquid and a lid helps prevent spilling. The shape must match what we want the object to do.

items.question: Draw a picture of a container that would be good for carrying water without spilling. Label the parts that help it work.

rubric.4: Clear drawing with labeled features explaining how shape prevents spilling (lid, handles, stable base)
rubric.3: Drawing with some labeled features related to function
rubric.2: Drawing of container but labels unclear or missing
rubric.1: Drawing present but not clearly a container or labeled

items.question: Two students made paper airplanes. One flew far and one flew short. What should they compare?
items.explanation: To understand why one plane flew better, we need to compare how they were made. The folds and shape affect how the plane flies.

items.question: Your class tested two different ramps to see which one made a ball roll farther. One ramp was tall, one was short. The tall ramp made the ball go farther. Draw both ramps and explain why you think the tall one worked better.

rubric.4: Both ramps drawn with clear height difference and explanation connecting height to ball speed/distance
rubric.3: Both ramps shown with some attempt at explanation
rubric.2: Ramps drawn but explanation missing or incorrect
